citations.assessment: The death scene names bar Natan as the one whose feet press onward, displacing Rav Ashi in the succession. Heilprin’s Ashi entry gives the same direction.
The folio gives Huna son of Rav Natan in a discussion of techum.
The folio gives Huna son of Rav Natan on an individual’s confession after prayer.
The Bavli states explicitly that Huna bar Natan deferred to Rav Ashi.
The parallel likewise names Huna as the person deferring.
Ashi quotes Huna’s question to Rava’s scribes. The checked reading has bar, where Heilprin prints ben in this notice.
Amemar permits the marriage and is the person whose basis was Zevid of Nehardea.
Huna relates the king adjusting his sash and quotes Amemar’s application of the Isaiah verse.
Rav Nachman reports Huna bar Natan deriving the requirement of ten for the wedding blessing.
The visit is to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak’s house. The group asks his name and he replies Rav Huna.
The group then asks why he calls himself Rav Huna. His reply concerns the title.
Rashi in the checked witness has Rav Huna, without ben. The attribution printed in Heilprin remains distinct.
Maharsha records Rashi’s childhood usage and quotes Yuchasin in Chananel’s name for the ordination explanation.
Pappa visits Huna bar Rav Natan. The objection is in the plural with no individual named.
Huna son of Rav Natan challenges Rav Pappa about Temple liquids.
Huna addresses Pappa about the Day of Atonement bull.
Huna speaks to Pappa about the scope of scriptural exclusion.
Huna directly responds to Pappa on the frontplate.
Huna answers the argument introduced by Rava across the folio break.
Rava introduces the proof to which Huna replies after the page break.
The succession narrative explicitly dates Ashi’s birth to the day Rava died.
The allusion repeats the succession direction. The proposed reason for longevity remains Heilprin’s suggestion.
The parallel explicitly places the pressure from bar Natan on Ashi.
Heilprin reports Huna deferring in the Ashi biography.
The father’s entry gives the relationship and distinct evidence for the father before Pappa.
Heilprin’s Ashi entry lists the name independently but does not establish the meaning of the Merimar pointer.
The later gloss explicitly gives approximately eighty years. Preserve its different estimate separately.
